projectState.overview: StreamTube is a YouTube-like video sharing platform built as an MBA greenfield challenge. Monorepo with NestJS 11 backend (nestjs-project/) and Next.js 16 frontend (next-frontend/). Phases 01 (base config) and 02 (auth — backend + frontend) are fully implemented and tested. Phase 03 (video upload and processing) is actively under implementation: SIs 03.1 through 03.6 are completed (Docker Compose infrastructure with Redis and MinIO, Video entity with migration, upload initiation, presign-part and abort multipart upload management, BullMQ queue setup, and upload complete endpoint). Next up are SI-03.7 through SI-03.9 (FFmpeg worker, streaming/download, and video metadata retrieval).

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 01 — Base Configuration
implementedFeatures.summary: Full project foundation: monorepo structure, NestJS 11 initialized, Docker Compose with PostgreSQL + Mailpit, TypeORM with DataSource and migration runner, environment validation via Joi, namespaced config with registerAs, Swagger/OpenAPI export, ESLint + Prettier.
implementedFeatures.notes: All services use Docker Compose service names as hosts (never localhost). Migrations run via npm run migration:run. Config organized per domain in src/config/ using registerAs factories.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 02 — Auth Backend (NestJS)
implementedFeatures.summary: Full authentication system: user registration with email confirmation, login with JWT access+refresh tokens, logout, forgot/reset password flow, channel auto-creation from email prefix. All flows tested with unit + integration + E2E tests.
implementedFeatures.notes: JWT stored in HttpOnly cookies. Refresh token rotation implemented. Channel nickname derived from email prefix. ChannelsService owns channel creation; UsersService compensates by deleting user if channel creation fails. Public decorator skips JWT guard. DomainException with custom filter.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 02 — Auth Frontend (Next.js)
implementedFeatures.summary: Auth screens built with Next.js App Router: signup, login, forgot-password. BFF API routes proxy to NestJS backend. Session managed via iron-session HttpOnly cookies. RHF + Zod validation. MSW mocks for all auth routes in test. Playwright E2E tests.
implementedFeatures.notes: OpenAPI types generated into lib/api/types.gen.ts. MSW enabled via MSW_ENABLED=true env var at server startup. Design system: Tailwind CSS 4, custom UI primitives in components/ui/. Playwright for E2E tests, Vitest for unit tests.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — Planning Artifacts
implementedFeatures.summary: All 6 technical decisions finalized, context document compiled, validation completed with clean status, and executable phase plan created with 9 SIs.
implementedFeatures.notes: TD-01 (BullMQ+Redis), TD-02 (S3 Multipart presigned URLs), TD-03 (Presigned GET 302 redirect), TD-04 (Separate worker container), TD-05 (nanoid 11 chars), TD-06 (Direct child_process for FFmpeg).

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — SI-03.1: Infrastructure (Redis, MinIO)
implementedFeatures.summary: Added Redis and MinIO services to compose.yaml. Created redisConfig and s3Config namespaced configs and validated environment variables with Joi.
implementedFeatures.notes: MinIO configured with local storage volumes, S3 port 9000, console 9001. Redis service on port 6379.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — SI-03.2: Video Entity, Migration & Module
implementedFeatures.summary: Implemented Video entity with VideoStatus enum, nanoid publicId, duration, storageKeys, thumbnail, and relation to Channel. Added migration 1792201054775-CreateVideos.ts and initialized VideosModule.
implementedFeatures.notes: Status transitions: DRAFT -> UPLOADING -> PROCESSING -> READY (or FAILED). Video linked to Channel entity via ManyToOne with onDelete CASCADE.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — SI-03.3: Initiate Upload (POST /videos)
implementedFeatures.summary: Implemented endpoint to initiate video creation and multipart upload with AWS S3 SDK (@aws-sdk/client-s3). Generates nanoid slug, creates DRAFT record, initiates multipart upload, transitions to UPLOADING, and returns uploadId + publicId.
implementedFeatures.notes: Requires authentication. Validates that authenticated user owns the destination channel. Uses StorageService wrapper for S3 CreateMultipartUploadCommand.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — SI-03.4: Upload Management (Presign-Part & Abort)
implementedFeatures.summary: Implemented POST /videos/:publicId/upload/part (presign upload part URL using @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner) and POST /videos/:publicId/upload/abort (aborts S3 multipart upload and marks video status FAILED).
implementedFeatures.notes: UploadPartCommand signed with expiry. AbortMultipartUploadCommand deletes pending S3 parts. Verifies video ownership and UPLOADING state.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — SI-03.5: BullMQ Queue Infrastructure
implementedFeatures.summary: Configured @nestjs/bullmq and BullMQ with Redis connection. Registered 'video-processing' queue in VideosModule. Added ioredis and resolved Jest ESM transformIgnorePatterns.
implementedFeatures.notes: BullModule.forRootAsync connected to Redis using redisConfig. Queue injected with @InjectQueue('video-processing').

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — SI-03.6: Complete Upload (POST /videos/:publicId/upload/complete)
implementedFeatures.summary: Implemented complete upload endpoint: finalizes S3 multipart upload via CompleteMultipartUploadCommand, transitions video status to PROCESSING, and enqueues job into 'video-processing' BullMQ queue.
implementedFeatures.notes: Payload accepts parts array with PartNumber and ETag. Verifies video status is UPLOADING and channel ownership before completing upload and enqueuing job.

conventionsAndPatterns: Docker Compose service names as hosts — never localhost/127.0.0.1 in config
NestJS modules: one module per domain, TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Entity]) in each module, never forRootAsync in feature modules
NestJS services: own only their domain's entities; cross-domain via service injection, not direct repository access
Config: @nestjs/config with namespaced registerAs(name, () => ({...})) factories — one file per domain in src/config/
Env validation: Joi schema in src/config/env.validation.ts passed to ConfigModule.forRoot
DomainException (common/exceptions/domain.exception.ts) for business rule violations, caught by DomainExceptionFilter
All NestJS routes protected by JwtAuthGuard globally; use @Public() decorator to expose public routes
Test file suffixes: .spec.ts (unit), .integration-spec.ts (integration), .e2e-spec.ts (E2E) — Jest filters by regex
Next.js BFF pattern: client calls /api/* route handlers, which forward to NestJS; client never calls NestJS directly
OpenAPI types: lib/api/types.gen.ts — regenerate after backend changes with openapi:export + openapi-typescript
MSW mocks: next-frontend/mocks/handlers/ — enabled via MSW_ENABLED=true env var (server-side MSW)
RHF + Zod for frontend forms; error mapping via lib/auth/error-mapping.ts
Git Flow: feature/* and bugfix/* branches from dev, merge to dev; dev → main when stable
Definition of Done: tests pass + full suite passes + tsc --noEmit exits 0 + npm run lint passes
